surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Pinto plays hero in overtime
paras: Shane Pinto got the scoring started for the Senators early in the first, and Tim Stützle made it 2-0 midway through the period. The Avalanche’s Nathan MacKinnon left in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. The Avs’ Cale Makar left in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. Artturi Lehkonen got the Avalanche on the board on the power play late in the period, and Parker Kelly tied it up shorthanded early in the third. Gabriel Landeskog put the Avalanche up 3-2 on the power play midway through the period. Drake Batherson tied it up for Ottawa with just under four minutes left. Pinto won it with his second goal of the night just over two minutes into overtime. He added an assist for a three-point night.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Linus Ullmark made 26 saves for the Senators, and Scott Wedgewood stopped 22 of 26 at the other end.
Brett Kulak took three penalties on his own. The Senators improved to 12-6-2, fourth in the Atlantic, while the Avalanche fell to 11-6-3, third in the Central.

items.text: The Senators won without William Eklund, Nick Cousins, Warren Foegele and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth and the Islanders were missing more at the time.
Thomas Chabot’s five-game point streak ended.
Philip Tomasino faces his old team, Pittsburgh, on Saturday.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
